newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ARS says may sign De Beers deal in 2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: ARS says may sign De Beers deal in 2 weeks.

text.p: Russia's largest diamond producer and sole authorised exporter could be ready to sign a new export deal with De Beers within two weeks, its first deputy director said on Thursday.

"We calculate that within two weeks the question will be decided and we will be able to have a final meeting to sign the agreement," Pavel Kovylin of Almazy Rossii Sakha (ARS, or Diamonds of Russia-Sakha) told Reuters.
But he said he considered his own view was optimistic and added that the process could take longer.
De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd's representatives in Moscow earlier in the week declined to comment on negotiations for a three year deal, except to repeat that talks have gone well.
Kovylin declined to comment on negotiation details but said he "had no reason to doubt" local press reports that a draft agreement had been approved by a few Russian ministries.

Russian newspapers reported that the Russian finance, economy, industry, and foreign economic relations ministries had approved a draft agreement which still had to pass other, unnamed, steps to receive full government approval.

Kovylin said deal negotiations, based on a February memorandum of understanding between ARS and De Beers under which De Beers will take half of Russia's rough diamond output, had dragged out over details.
"It took time to work out technical details, a more practical understanding, after the general understanding of the memorandum," he said.
